summary.text: Katie Hobbs is the Democratic Governor of Arizona and won re-election on November 3, 2026, with John Giles, the former mayor of Mesa, as her running mate.
A social worker by training, she served in the Arizona House and Senate and as Secretary of State before being elected governor in 2022.

paragraphs.text: Hobbs was born in Phoenix and raised in Tempe.

She earned a bachelor's degree in social work from Northern Arizona University in 1992 and a master's in social work from Arizona State University in 1995, and according to the governor's office put herself through college.
She worked as a social worker and as chief compliance officer at the Sojourner Center, a domestic violence shelter, and was executive director of Emerge Arizona from 2013 to 2019.
Hobbs served one term in the Arizona House, elected in 2010, and three terms in the Arizona Senate, elected in 2012, 2014 and 2016, becoming Senate Minority Leader in 2015.
She was Arizona Secretary of State from January 2019 until she became governor in January 2023.
Katie Hobbs won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election for governor with 55.6% of the vote to Andy Biggs's 42.5%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
